answer: An exact sensor configuration should not be fixed yet, because the contaminant and the quality variable are unknown. The first step is a lab test of paired in-specification and off-specification liquid samples, with NIR transmission/transflection as the main method and Raman and MIR ATR as comparison methods. The independent laboratory analyses then define the target and show which method, or which combination, sees the difference.

inline.headline: Test NIR transmission/transflection on paired in-specification and off-specification liquid samples before fixing any exact sensor configuration
inline.probe: NIR transmission/transflection probe for liquids (path 1–10 mm)
inline.install: At the process point where the off-specification liquid can be measured in flow; the location is not yet known
inline.test_against: Raman probe (liquid, 2–5 mm) on the same samples
inline.not_final_because: The contaminant and quality variable are unknown, the liquid's transparency and path length are not known, and NIR alone may lack sensitivity to low-level components below about 0.1 %.

problems.text: An exact sensor configuration cannot be chosen before the analytical problem is known; the contaminant and quality variable are unknown, and for samples of unknown composition several methods are tested first.

Assuming one spectroscopy method will see the contaminant is not safe when the contaminant is unknown; fluorescence only sees substances that emit secondary light, and most chemicals do not fluoresce.
NIR alone may miss a contaminant present at trace level, because NIR may lack sensitivity below about 0.1 %.

methods.why: Suited to liquids with a 1–10 mm path, the most common online fiber-probe method, and works with remote fiber probes.
Recorded in the visible/NIR region with high selectivity and information complementary to MIR; signals are weak and can be masked by fluorescence.
Well-defined absorption peaks for liquids at a 1–6 µm depth; ATR fiber probes analyse liquids at a distance from the spectrometer.
Highly sensitive, but only for substances that emit secondary light, mostly of biological origin; use only if the contaminant is shown to fluoresce.

questions.q: Which quality variable goes off specification, and what are its specification limits?
questions.why: The target must be defined before a method can be selected.

questions.q: Can you supply paired in-specification and off-specification samples, with independent laboratory analysis of the suspected contaminant or quality variable?
questions.why: Laboratory results are the reference for the test; the instrument cannot calibrate itself.

questions.q: Is the liquid transparent, turbid or opaque, and what is its colour?
questions.why: Transparency sets the probe type and path length; opaque or turbid liquids need a reflection or ATR approach.

questions.q: Where in the process does the off-specification occur, and can a probe be installed at that point?
questions.why: The install point and the interface depend on the process location.

experiment.objective: Find which method, if any, sees the difference between in-specification and off-specification liquid before any exact sensor configuration is fixed.
steps: Collect paired in-specification and off-specification samples, with the quality limits and the suspected contaminant named by the client.
Measure all samples with a NIR transmission/transflection probe and a Raman probe, in the same batch and time window.
Send the same samples to an independent laboratory for the contaminant or quality variable; these results are the reference.
Check that the fiber covers the measured range: Vis-NIR silica (350–2400 nm) for NIR, and for Raman use 785 nm excitation with the Raman shift in cm-1.
Run PCA on the spectra, then compare a fused NIR + Raman model with the best single method on the same validation samples.
references: Independent laboratory analysis of the suspected contaminant or quality variable
AFS multi-method lab test (step 1 of the AFS pathway)
experiment.go_no_go: Criteria come from the client: the quality limits and the required detection level, which the client has not yet given. Go only if a method separates in-specification from off-specification samples on the independent reference data.

pathway.key_features: Not yet known; to be selected from the lab spectra by multivariate analysis, as the bands that separate in-specification from off-specification samples.
pathway.path_reason: The contaminant and quality variable are unknown; the AFS pathway starts with a multi-method lab test before any solution is chosen.

multispectral.why: NIR sees hydrogen bonds and polar groups, while Raman sees the molecular backbone and non-polar groups, so their information is complementary; NIR + Raman gave the best result in the pellet coating process.
multispectral.test: Run NIR alone, Raman alone and the fused NIR + Raman model on the same paired samples; keep the combination only if its validation result beats the best single method.
